name: Cobalt sulfate; at plant
description: The functional unit for this model is one kilogram of cobalt sulfate. The technical scope includes the gate-to-gate production of cobalt sulfate. The system boundary includes incoming transport, manufacturing, and disposal of process wastes. Incoming crude cobalt hydroxide, 35% cobalt content, is produced in the Democratic Republic of Congo and is then sent to China for further refining. Data were provided by the top three refined cobalt producers in China, Huayou Cobalt, GEM, and Jinchuan, which accounted for over 60% of China’s total refined cobalt output in 2016. This model relies upon data from the Tongxiang plant of Huayou cobalt. Please see the data selection field for more details on how this data was chosen.

processDocumentation.timeDescription: This unit process is representative of operations in 2016. Data are applicable for the next 10 years after 2017, i.e., 2027.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: This unit process is representative of cobalt sulfate production in China.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription:
Purchased crude cobalt hydroxide is treated with sulfuric acid first, which leaches cobalt out as CoSO4.  Sodium metabisulfite (Na2S2O5) is added to the leaching step also, to convert remaining Co3+ into Co2+. 
The leached solution then undergoes several precipitation steps to remove iron and aluminum, solvent extraction by P204 to remove other impurities, another solvent extraction by P207 to separate cobalt from nickel, stripping by sulfuric acid to produce refined CoSO4, and finally evaporation and crystallization followed by filtration and drying to produce battery-grade CoSO4 crystals.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: The estimated material and energy flows for the Tongxiang plant of Huayou Cobalt, after its expansion, were chosen in this study to represent battery-grade cobalt sulfate production. Steam use at the Tongxiang plant was converted into natural gas use for GREET implementation.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Elementary flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. Technosphere flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. The mass balance for this process was not calculated
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription:
The estimated material and energy flows for the Tongxiang plant (after the expansion) were chosen in this study to represent battery-grade CoSO4 cobalt sulfate production. The GEM plant data were excluded because material and energy flows specific to cobalt sulfate production were not reported by GEM. Refined cobalt production at Jinchuan is not included in this study, either, due to lack of data. 
In 2016, an expansion project of the Tongxiang plant of Huayou Cobalt was underway. After the expansion, the plant uses crude Co(OH)2 as the only cobalt feed, which aligns well with the assumption of this analysis. The estimated material and energy flows for the Tongxiang plant after the expansion were chosen in this study to represent battery-grade CoSO4 production. Steam use at the Tongxiang plant was converted into natural gas use for GREET implementation.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Steam use at the Tongxiang plant was converted into natural gas use for GREET.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription:
The system boundary includes incoming transport, manufacturing, and disposal of process wastes. 
The estimated material and energy flows for the Tongxiang plant after the expansion were chosen in this study to represent battery-grade CoSO4 production. Uncertainty was not calculated.

sources.name: Cobalt Life Cycle Analysis Update for the GREET® Model, 2018

reviews.details: Independent internal review was performed by Argonne National Lab.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication: Situation C1 - Accounting, with system-external interactions - The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system including existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model. The target audience of this model includes LCA practitioners, industry, and the general public. The direct emissions associated with this dataset come from GREET which considers greenhouse gases, water consumption, and criteria air pollutants, including VOCs, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, particulate matter, and sulfur oxides. Therefore, the following TRACI impact categories are compatible with this dataset: global warming potential, smog formation, and human health – particulate matter. It may be compatible with additional impact categories.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: This project was funded by DOE. These data are cradle-to-gate LCIs for the production of refined cobalt and cobalt chemicals by production stages, which was an update for the GREET model. 2018.

publication.name: Cobalt Life Cycle Analysis Update for the GREET® Model, 2018
